coverage.surface: Pilot Desk default screen (v4) — all five steps, participant band, participant gaps, participant materials, check-in log, adoption review, results summary, toasts
coverage.note: Read every string and branch in source. Rendered evidence from the SMB walkthrough (today) and the enterprise walkthrough (2026-11-06) covers only the at-rest state and the deal picker; steps 2-5, the materials list, gap drawer, check-in log and toasts are not in either walkthrough (seeded pilot data never loads — see finding on demo seed), so those states are source-reviewed only.

findings.state: Step 3 'Monitor pilot engagement' panel, under the 'Participants using it' / 'Actions recorded' counters
findings.current: Usage can come from product telemetry or be marked manually above.
findings.problem: CLAIM / declarative certainty. Nothing in Pilot Desk reads product telemetry: `active` is only set by clicking a participant's name (toggleActive, line 211) and `actions` is only the number typed into the 'actions this check-in' box (logCheckIn, line 268). A seller will look for a telemetry connection that does not exist, or assume the counts are measured. The type comment at src/pilot-desk/v4/lib/pilot.ts:28 ('from the product's usage, or by hand') repeats the same unsupported claim for future writers.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (claims discipline: copy must not assert behavior the code does not have); COPY_STANDARD.md §21
findings.proposed: Replace with: "Mark each participant as using the product by clicking their name above. Enter the number of actions from your own usage report when you log a check-in." Also change the comment at v4/lib/pilot.ts:28 to "Actions taken this check-in, entered by the seller." OWNER DECISION: if usage should really come from the vendor product's telemetry, that is a new integration; until it exists the screen must say counts are entered by hand.

findings.state: Step 4 'Review adoption' panel headline, chosen by readAdoption() band (src/pilot-desk/v4/lib/pilot.ts:212-224)
findings.current: ready: "Adoption is sufficient for the current evaluation." / almost: "Adoption is close to the current threshold. One additional active participant would improve the evaluation." / thin: "Adoption is currently too limited to evaluate the pilot fairly."
findings.problem: Declarative certainty + high-context dependence. (1) 'the current threshold' is never stated; the rule is: ready = at least two-thirds of hands-on participants marked active AND more than 0 actions at the last check-in; almost = at least half active. (2) The 'almost' message is wrong in a reachable case: every participant is active but the last check-in recorded 0 actions → band 'almost' → the screen tells the seller to add one more active participant, when the missing condition is recorded actions. A first-time user is told to do the wrong thing.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (state the reasoning: evidence → interpretation → action); COPY_STANDARD.md §6, §7, §21; Batch 02 structural requirement 'Pilot Desk: … engagement, adoption'
findings.proposed: Build the headline from the AdoptionRead fields instead of the band alone: ready → "{using} of {enrolled} hands-on participants are using the product and {actionsLast} actions were recorded at the last check-in. That meets the adoption threshold (two-thirds of participants, with recorded actions)."; using/enrolled ≥ 1/2 but < 2/3 → "{using} of {enrolled} hands-on participants are using the product. The threshold is two-thirds, so one more active participant would meet it." (compute the real shortfall); all active but actionsLast = 0 → "Participants are marked as using the product, but no actions were recorded at the last check-in. Log a check-in with the action count."; otherwise → "{using} of {enrolled} hands-on participants are using the product. That is too few to evaluate the pilot fairly."

findings.state: Potential participant gaps → 'Add person →' → 'Ask the champion for an introduction' (copied to clipboard)
findings.current: `${champion?.name ?? "Hi"} — for the pilot we still need ${g.q.toLowerCase()} involved. Who owns this on your side, and would you introduce us?` → for the IT gap this produces "… for the pilot we still need it or data owner involved. …"
findings.problem: Runtime-built message sent to a buyer is garbled: lower-casing the label 'IT or data owner' turns the acronym into the word 'it' and drops the article ('need it or data owner involved'). The second gap produces 'need day-to-day pilot owner involved' (no article). The seller pastes this to the champion.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (elliptical syntax / meaning lost in generation)
findings.proposed: Give each gap its own phrase instead of lower-casing the label, e.g. add `ask: "someone from IT or the data owner"` and `ask: "a day-to-day pilot owner"` to the gap objects (lines 256-265) and build: `${champion?.name ?? "Hi"} — for the pilot we still need ${g.ask} involved. Who owns this on your side, and would you introduce us?`

findings.state: Participant materials → FAQ → 'Send →' (copies the template to the clipboard for the seller to send to buyer participants)
findings.current: Short FAQ: What happens to our data? Nothing leaves your environment. Does this replace our stack? No — it sits on top. What if it doesn't work? We stop at the agreed date.
findings.problem: Unsupported certainty about the seller's own product. Antaeus does not know where the seller's product stores data or whether it replaces anything, yet the template asserts 'Nothing leaves your environment' and 'it sits on top' as fact for the seller to forward to a buyer. A first-time seller copying it could send a false security claim.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (declarative certainty); COPY_STANDARD.md §21; original-working-set/11_AI_PROMPT_AND_GENERATOR_REWRITE_SPEC.md (no invented facts in generated output)
findings.proposed: Short FAQ: What happens to our data? [Describe where pilot data is stored and who can access it.] Does this replace our current tools? [Explain how it works alongside them.] What if it doesn't work? We stop on the agreed end date and review the results together.

findings.state: Participant materials list — each item's button
findings.current: Buttons read "Send →" / "Ask →" / "Copy →" / "Build together →" (KIT verbs, lines 118-182); after clicking, the button reads "Sent ✓" and the toast says "Copied."
findings.problem: The action only copies a draft message to the clipboard (copyText, line 397) and records the key in `shared`. Nothing is sent, so 'Sent ✓' asserts something that did not happen and 'Send →' / 'Build together →' describe actions the button does not perform. A seller who clicks and moves on believes the participants have the material.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (copy must describe what the control does); COPY_STANDARD.md §21
findings.proposed: Use "Copy message →" for every item ("Copy plan →" for the pilot plan) and, after clicking, "Copied ✓" (or "Marked as shared ✓" if the `shared` list is meant to record that the seller sent it). Keep the `shared` keys unchanged.

findings.current: Team — we're piloting a new tool for the next two weeks at ${c.account}. …
findings.problem: Hard-coded 'two weeks' while the pilot length is chosen as 7 or 14 days (setDurationDays). On a 7-day pilot the announcement states the wrong length.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (generated text must match the data)
findings.proposed: Pass the pilot length into the template context and write: "Team — we're piloting a new tool at ${c.account} for the next ${c.days} days. …" (ctx.days = draft.durationDays).

findings.state: Top of page: deal picker; participant row controls
findings.current: <select class="pk4-dealsel"> has no label or aria-label (walkthrough: "(unlabelled field)"); participant 'Name'/'role' inputs are placeholder-only (lines 327-328); the participant-type <select> (line 329) is unlabelled; the remove button is a bare "×" (line 323); participant names toggle 'using it' via onClick on a <span> (line 319), so the toggle is unreachable by keyboard and has no role.
findings.problem: Screen-reader users hear an unnamed combobox and an unnamed '×'; keyboard users cannot mark a participant active, which is the only way adoption gets recorded.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (accessible names); SMB walkthrough '1. The area at rest | field] (unlabelled field)'
findings.proposed: aria-label="Link this pilot to a deal" on the deal select; aria-label="Participant name", "Participant role", "Participant type" on the add-row controls; aria-label={`Remove ${p.name}`} on the × button; render the participant name as a <button type="button" aria-pressed={p.active}> (or add role="button" tabIndex={0} and Enter/Space handling) with the existing title as its description.

findings.state: Demo book (SMB and enterprise) → Pilot Desk → choose the seeded pilot deal (Notion / Sweetgreen; OpenAI / Boeing)
findings.current: Seed writes gtmos_poc_data rows with legacy field names {success, duration, created} (smb 449-451, ent js/demo-seed-data-ent.js:638-640) and gtmos_pilot_desk_v1 keyed by lower-case account name ('notion', 'sweetgreen', 'boeing', 'openai'; smb 456, ent 646), with shared keys ['getting_started','role_quickstarts','champion_kit','kickoff_note','case_study'], closedGaps ['it_person','second_site'], and check-ins oldest-first.
findings.problem: None of it reaches the screen. parseProof (src/pilot-desk/lib/persistence.ts:62-101) reads successCriteria/durationDays/updatedAt, so seeded criteria are empty, the 14/21-day lengths become 7, and updatedAt becomes 'now' — both walkthroughs show only "Day 1 of 7" for Notion/OpenAI. The v4 page keys pilot extras by linked deal id first (extrasKey, PilotDeskV4.tsx:60-63), so the account-keyed participant groups, check-ins and the Sweetgreen/Boeing results summaries never load when the deal is chosen. The material keys and gap ids do not match KIT keys ('video','quickstart','champion','kickoff','case') or gap ids ('it','driver'), and readAdoption treats checkins[0] as the latest. The tester never sees steps 2-5 populated, so the demo hides the area's main workflow.
findings.governing: comprehension principle; original-working-set/01_OWNER_REQUIREMENTS.md required work 5 (seeded narratives) and 8 (regenerate the demo-seeded tester pathway)
findings.proposed: In js/demo-seed-data-smb.js and js/demo-seed-data-ent.js: write pocs as {id, account, vendor, readoutOwner, linkedDealId:'deal_s_notion'…, durationDays:14, outcome, successCriteria, boundaries, updatedAt}; key pilotDesk by the deal id ('deal_s_notion', 'deal_s_sweetgreen', 'deal_e_openai', 'deal_e_boeing'); use shared keys from the KIT list and closedGaps ['it']; order check-ins newest first; use 14 instead of 21 for OpenAI (DurationDays is 7 | 14). Add a seed-shape test that loads each book through loadProofs/loadExtras.

findings.state: Seller types an account, adds participants / logs check-ins, then links the deal from the picker (or arrives later with ?deal=)
findings.current: extrasKey() returns linkedDealId when set, else the account name; the effect at lines 83-89 reloads extras from the new key when it changes.
findings.problem: Participants, check-ins and the results summary saved under the account-name key disappear from the screen as soon as the deal is linked, because loadExtras(dealId) finds nothing; the data is orphaned in gtmos_pilot_desk_v1. Once linked, the picker is replaced by a link (line 288), so there is no way back.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (saved work must stay visible); CLAUDE.md Part III §3 rule 5
findings.proposed: In the key-switch effect, when the new key is a deal id and loadExtras(newKey) is empty but loadExtras(draft.account) is not, copy the account-keyed extras to the deal-id key (saveExtras) before assigning. Optionally keep a small 'Change deal' control next to the deal link.

findings.state: Step 3 check-in step list, second step when every enrolled participant is active
findings.current: Everyone enrolled is using it. Pull in the next person from their side — another user or the person who signs off.
findings.problem: Casual stand-ins ('it', 'pull in', 'from their side', 'the person who signs off') where the page elsewhere uses 'participants', 'the product' and 'approves the result'; reads as a fragment pair rather than an action the seller checks off.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §26 (name the thing instead of a casual stand-in); Batch 02 structural requirement 'approver'
findings.proposed: All enrolled participants are using the product. Decide whether to add another user or the person who approves the result.
